findings.title: Round 18 USB-only UART rule is keyed to the inverted TPS2121 status polarity: U11 IN1 is USB, not the battery

evidence.text: Enable the UARTs only when PA4 (LOGIC_SOURCE_ST) shows U11's IN1 (the battery) selected, after a settling delay, and park PC6 and PB13 again when PA4 falls or the PA6 shedding trigger fires.

evidence.file: native netlist (kicad-cli 10.0.7 export, equal to schematic.net.xml) and board
evidence.measured: U11.7 symbol pin IN1_USB = USB_LIMITED (pad (24.3,63.825)); U11.2 IN2_BAT = RAW_PROTECTED (pad (24.3,65.175)); U11.6 PR1 = GND; U11.3 CP2 = GND; U11.9 ST = LOGIC_SOURCE_ST -> U1.28 PA4 (30.55,48.0) with R91 10 kohm to 3V3 at B(28.1,60.0)

evidence.pages: p4 pin functions: RUX pin 7 = IN1, pin 2 = IN2, pin 9 = ST; p18 Table 9-3: with CP2 and PR1 low (VCOMP mode) IN2 >= IN1 -> OUT = IN2, ST = L; IN2 invalid -> OUT = IN1, ST = H; 'ST is pulled high when the output is Hi-Z or IN1. It is pulled low when IN2 is powering the output'; p21 'If the status pin is high, IN1 is the output. If the pin is low, IN2 is the output'

evidence.text: U11 IN1=USB_LIMITED, IN2=RAW_PROTECTED ... ST LOW = IN2 battery. ST HIGH = IN1 USB OR both sources invalid

origin of the error: 'U11 TPS2121 ... IN1 pin 2 RAW_PROTECTED, IN2 pin 7 USB_LIMITED' and 'use PA4/LOGIC_SOURCE_ST high (TPS2121 IN1 selected) ... park ... on PA4 falling' (pins swapped against SLVSEA3F p4)

evidence.pointers: /port_states/startup and /firmware_obligations/19 give no battery-path test for 'ports powered'; /port_states/shutdown_shedding and obligation 12 stop the UARTs but do not park PC6/PB13; /firmware_obligations/14 still says 'GPS/radio are always powered'
evidence.note: pin_table rows 52/63 say 'park as an input (no pull) or drive it low'; M3_R10 and ORDERING 8.3 say 'analog'

findings.impact: Documentation defect in the firmware obligations (no firmware exists; hardware is correct). Implemented as written, the rule inverts R18-MCU-02's intent: with the pack on (U11 IN2, ST low) the GPS and radio UARTs would never be enabled, so no GPS or telemetry on battery power (REQUIREMENTS F10), and with USB only (IN1, ST high) the UARTs would be enabled with TX idle-high into the unpowered modules (about 2.7 mA per line through 1 kohm), the back-drive the rule was written to prevent. 'Park when PA4 falls' parks exactly when the battery path comes on.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only, no CAD: in docs/M3_R10.md replace the sentence with 'Enable the GPS and radio UARTs only while PA4 (LOGIC_SOURCE_ST) reads low, i.e. U11 has selected IN2 = RAW_PROTECTED, the battery path (TI SLVSEA3F Table 9-3 p18; ST is high for IN1 = USB or no valid input), after a settling delay; park PC6 and PB13 in analog mode with no pull when PA4 rises or the PA6 shedding trigger fires.' Carry the same PA4-low condition and the park step into the binding note (port_states.startup, shutdown_shedding, obligations 12 and 19; regenerate with r10_sch_check.py --binding-note) and change obligation 14's 'GPS/radio are always powered' to 'GPS/radio stay powered whenever the battery path is on (firmware cannot switch them)'. Use one parking mode (analog, no pull) in pin_table rows 52/63, M3_R10 and ORDERING 8.3. Optional, owner decision: the same PA4-low test can gate PC1 (refuse the load-switch enable while PA4 is high), which blocks the documented USB-powered, switch-open case in firmware (it does not cover back-feed from a self-powered module).

findings.title: DS12110 cites in the pin table and binding note mix revisions and electrical sections; several page and note cites cannot all be right

evidence.source: DS12110 Rev 8 (only copy reachable: the repository cache and the LCSC mirror are byte-identical, SHA-256 0c4f0169...cafc; st.com timed out on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 and via WebFetch)
evidence.measured: Rev 8 has two electrical chapters: section 6 'Electrical characteristics (rev Y)' pp104-209 and section 7 '(rev V)' pp210-320. Port AF tables are Tables 10-14 on pp89-96.

cite rev Y tables: Table 60 p139 (RPU), Table 61 p141 (VOH), Tables 28-29 pp111-112 (VREFINT), Table 94 p180 (VBAT/4). The binding note's other cites (Rev 11 Tables 109/112/136/147/149/150) are the rev V chapter (Rev 8 Tables 119/122/146/157/159/160). Rev V equivalents: Table 157 p246, Table 158 p248, Tables 127-128 pp218-219, Table 192 p293. Values compared: identical (RPU 30/40/50 kohm, VOH >= VDD-0.4 V at -8 mA, VREFINT 1.180/1.216/1.255 V, VREFIN_CAL 0x1FF1E860, VBAT ratio error +/-10 %).

several unchanged AF page cites are one page below Rev 8 (PB2 p. 90 is not): PA0-PA3, PA11, PA12 'Table 10 p. 88' (Rev 8 p89); PA13, PA14, PB3-PB6 'p. 89' (p90); PB8/PB9 'p. 90' (p91); PD11-PD13 'p. 93' (p94); PE2 'p. 94' (p95); PE7/PE8 'pp. 89-94' (p95, outside the range). The rows harmonised in 1e60441 cite PB12/PB13 p. 91 and PC6/PC7/PC10-PC12 p. 92, equal to Rev 8. In Rev 8, PB8/PB9 and PB12/PB13 sit on the same page (p91, Table 11 continued, page image af-091.png); the table puts them on p90 and p91 of one 'Table 10'.

evidence.file: pin_table.tsv rows 51-52, 63-64; binding obligation 14; telemetry.kicad_sch note
evidence.measured: 'Table 147 note 6 p. 242' for the pull-off rule: in Rev 8 that rule is Table 157 note 7 (p247); note 6 there is 'VIN must be less than Max(VDDXXX) + 3.6 V'. 'Table 112 note 3' matches Rev 8 Table 122 note 3 (p215).
still cite 'Rev10' tables (row 7: 'Table63 note 2 pp142-143', a rev Y table) while the binding note cites the same 2 MHz limit as Rev 11 Table 150 note 2 p246.

findings.impact: Evidence and navigation only. Every pin, AF, ADC channel and parameter this lens relies on was checked against Rev 8 and is correct; no numeric consequence (rev Y and rev V values are identical for the cited parameters). The Rev 11 numbers remain an Inference, as D-R18-10 already states.
findings.concrete_fix: When st.com is reachable, do one cite pass against a single DS12110 revision: cite the rev V chapter consistently (the design's conditional basis), re-read the page and note numbers for every AF row and for the pull-off note, and record the revision and download date in the binding note sources. No CAD change.

findings.title: Two retained R8-era schematic notes contradict the R10 MCU map (camera OE on PA7; sentinels driven low)

evidence.text: 'R8: PE8/pin38 UART7_TX and PE7/pin37 UART7_RX use AF7 ... PA7/pin31 controls OE as GPIO.'
evidence.netlist: U12.6 OE = CAM_UART_OE = U1.39 PE9 with R102 10 kohm to GND; U1.31 PA7 has no net (pin_table row 31: 'CAM_UART_OE moved to PE9, D-R2-07')

evidence.text: 'R2: PE3 (pin 2) and PE6 (pin 5) are pyro-gate sentinels - no net, firmware drives them low.'
evidence.conflict: pin_table rows 2/4/5 and binding obligation 5: 'Keep sentinel pins PE3/PE5/PE6/PC4 without nets and in analog mode ..., never driven' (R5-MCU-03); PE4's neighbours are PE3 (pin 2) and PE5 (pin 4), not PE6

evidence.generator: m3_design/r10_sch.py retains R8 notes (r8_sch.py lines 214-216, 249-251); R18's R10_MCU_NOTES replaced three mcu-sheet notes but not these two
evidence.prior_reviews: no round 10-18 report mentions either note (searched)

findings.impact: Documentation defect in the schematic, which AGENTS section 3 makes the source of truth. A firmware author following the camera note would drive PA7 and leave PE9 analog, so R102 keeps the camera UART isolated (function lost, not a hazard). Following the sentinel note would drive PE3 low; a PE3-PE4 solder bridge (0.2 mm pin gap) would then fight the fire command instead of floating (fire inhibited; no inadvertent fire).
findings.concrete_fix: In m3_design/r10_sch.py (as R18 did with R10_MCU_NOTES), replace the camera_uart note's last sentence with 'PE9/pin39 CAM_UART_OE controls OE as GPIO; R102 10 k holds it low.' and the mcu note's first sentence with 'PE3 (pin 2) and PE5 (pin 4) flank PE4: no net, analog, never driven (R5-MCU-03).', keeping the R8 LED sentence; fix the check_actuators.py comment; regenerate the sheets. Netlist, binding hashes and board are unchanged.

findings.title: No firmware obligation keeps the internal VREFBUF disabled although VREF+ is hard-wired to VDDA (3V3A, the sensor rail)

evidence.netlist: U1.20 VREF+ and U1.21 VDDA both on 3V3A = 3V3 through R164 2.2 ohm (B(17.325,55.9)), with C21 100 nF (1.47-1.76 mm) and C22 1 uF; 3V3A also supplies U4 (VDD/VDDIO) and U5 (VDD, PS)

evidence.pages: Figure 95 p285 'Power supply and reference decoupling (VREF+ connected to VDDA)' (supported); Table 189 pp291-292 VREFBUF output 2.5/2.049/1.804/1.5015 V, static load <= 4 mA; Table 9 note 7 p88: where VREF+ is double-bonded to VDDA (TFBGA100) 'the internal voltage reference buffer is not available and must be kept disabled'

evidence.maker: ST SVD STM32H743 v2.4 (modm-io mirror) and cmsis-svd-data STM32H743x
evidence.measured: VREFBUF_CSR reset 0x00000002 (HIZ = 1, ENVR = 0: external VREF+ mode at reset)

evidence.lines: 530-542: HAL_SYSCFG_VREFBUF_HighImpedanceConfig DISABLE = 'VREF+ pin is internally connect to VREFINT output'; 561-565 HAL_SYSCFG_EnableVREFBUF sets ENVR

evidence.records: grep of docs/, r10_binding_note.json, pin_table.tsv, schematic notes: no VREFBUF or VREF+ mode rule (obligation 20 reads VDDA from VREFINT only)

findings.impact: Bounded firmware-obligation gap; the reset state is correct. A firmware that enables the buffer (one HAL call) would connect a 1.5-2.5 V regulator output to a pin held at about 3.3 V by 3V3A through 2.2 ohm, outside the buffer's specified load (Inference: RM0433's VREFBUF mode table not re-read), and any code that then assumes VREF+ = 2.5 V scales every ADC reading (continuity, bus, PA6 shedding) by about 0.76.
findings.concrete_fix: Add one binding-note obligation and a line under M3_R10 'Sensors': 'VREF+ is tied to VDDA (3V3A): keep VREFBUF_CSR at its reset value (ENVR = 0, HIZ = 1, external reference); never call HAL_SYSCFG_EnableVREFBUF or clear HIZ; scale the ADC from VREFINT / VREFIN_CAL.' Can ride on the same binding-note regeneration as R19-MCU-01. No CAD change.

fix_verification.claim: R123 100 k -> 2 k (C4109, same land) keeps Q122 off against a PC1 pull-up and still turns it on: gate 2.19 V nominal, 1.92 V at the VOH floor; <= 0.220 V against 30 kohm at 3.6 V
fix_verification.measurement: Board: R123 2k, LCSC C4109 / 0402WGF2001TCE, F(20.6,70.66) rot -90, pads ACT_EN / GND; JLC BOM line C4109 x5 includes R123; parts_budget values 2.1853 / 1.9204 / 0.2203 V reproduced (calcs.json). With AP63203 VFB minimum 3.27 V (Diodes DS41326 Rev 3-2 p5, CCM, -40..85 C) the VOH floor (DS12110 Rev 8 Table 158 p248: VDD-0.4 V at -8 mA; PC1 sources 1.1 mA) gives 1.900 V, 0.45 V above AO3400A VGS(th) max 1.45 V (Rev 3.1 p2). Q122's initial drain current is 0.84 mA while C120 discharges (8.4 V / R121), settling to 0.14 mA; saturation at 1.90-2.19 V stays Inference, as recorded. A BAT_ENABLE bridge at R123.1 (0.330 mm) now holds U9 off (fail-safe), where 100 k gave about 0.8 V at the Q122 gate.

fix_verification.claim: V3V3_SENSE (R62/R63) removed; PC3_C (U1.18) NC; VDDA from VREFINT and 3V3 from VBAT/4
fix_verification.measurement: R62/R63 absent; U1.18 pad (25.5,50.55) has no net and no track or via (33 U1 NC pads; 100/100 pins agree across board, fresh netlist, pin_table and binding note). LQFP100 PC3_C is joined to GPIO PC3 by the SYSCFG_PMCR analog switch (DS12110 Rev 8 Table 9 note 6 p88); ST's SVD lists PMCR reset 0x00000000 (switch closed; HAL: PC3SO = 1 opens) and GPIO PC3 resets to analog (DS section 3.8 p32), so the floating pad has no enabled digital input in either switch state; 'analog, never driven' is sufficient. The removed divider read 0.5007-0.5034 of full scale for 2-10 mA of 3V3A load, so it carried no 3V3 information. Note: VBAT/4 is also ratiometric to VREF+ and has a +/-10 % ratio error (Rev 8 Table 94 p180 / Table 192 p293), so the 3V3 figure really comes from VREFINT (3V3A is 3V3 minus mV across R164).

fix_verification.claim: ACT_EN_MCU 0.550 mm to BAT_FAULT_N, 0.520 mm to LS120.2, 0.425 mm NRST via, GND 0.251 mm, U1.15/U1.17 0.200 mm; ACT_EN-BAT_ENABLE 0.330 mm
